provenance.source: Created for this repository example; no external dataset, user records, model outputs, or human annotators.
provenance.labels: candidate and weak are construction roles, not independently validated human quality labels. No calibration labels are supplied.
provenance.purpose: Expose configured MockJudge failure modes and keyword-scoring blind spots; not a benchmark of deployed LLMs.

groups.semantic_rubric: Explain the fictional returns policy: verify a receipt, check the 30-day window, refund to the original payment method, and escalate exceptions. Do not invent an approval.

cases.prompt: A customer returns an unused item after 14 days with proof of purchase. What should support do?
cases.candidate: Check the receipt and window before refunding the original payment method.

cases.prompt: A customer asks for a return after 45 days. What should support do?
cases.candidate: The window has passed. Check the receipt and request escalation for an exception.

cases.prompt: An unused item arrives without proof of purchase. What should support do?
cases.candidate: Request the receipt and check the window. Use escalation if proof cannot be recovered.

cases.prompt: A customer has replaced the card used for an eligible purchase. What should support do?
cases.candidate: Verify the receipt and original payment method. Request escalation for the changed card.
cases.weak: Refund to any account they provide.

groups.semantic_rubric: Summarize only the fictional incident facts in the prompt: timeline, customer impact, mitigation, and evidence. Mark missing facts as unknown; do not claim a root cause.

cases.prompt: At 09:10 a deploy began; at 09:12 API errors rose; a rollback at 09:20 reduced errors. Root cause is unknown.
cases.candidate: The timeline links the deploy and errors. Describe impact cautiously and record rollback mitigation.

cases.prompt: Queue delay rose at 16:00; workers were increased at 16:15; no recovery measurement exists yet.
cases.candidate: Record the timeline and worker mitigation. Recovery needs evidence before claiming success.

cases.prompt: Two customers saw stale pages; the cache was cleared; onset time is not recorded.
cases.candidate: Record the impact and cache mitigation. The timeline has an unknown start.

cases.prompt: An alert reports p95 latency at 900 ms; there are no customer reports or mitigation notes.
cases.candidate: Record the alert evidence and latency impact. The mitigation is unknown.

groups.semantic_rubric: Summarize only the fictional study facts: source, sample, uncertainty, and limitations. Distinguish association from causation and do not generalize beyond the sample.

cases.prompt: An internal survey of 18 volunteers reports a preference for interface A. There is no randomized assignment.
cases.candidate: Name the source and sample. State uncertainty about whether the preference generalizes.
cases.weak: Interface A is proven best for everyone.

cases.prompt: A pilot team reports faster completion after a workflow change, with no control group.
cases.candidate: Name the source and limitations. State uncertainty about attributing the change to the workflow.
cases.weak: The workflow caused a universal productivity gain.

cases.prompt: A blog post claims users like a feature but provides no participant count or study method.
cases.candidate: Identify the source and unknown sample. State limitations from the missing method.
cases.weak: The feature has statistically proven demand.

cases.prompt: A single office tests a prototype for one week; results from other offices are unavailable.
cases.candidate: Describe the sample and short duration limitations. Preserve uncertainty about other offices.
cases.weak: Roll out everywhere because success is guaranteed.
